contents.text: In a chemical reaction, the starting molecules, or reactants, are converted into new molecules, or products. To understand how enzymes speed up chemical reactions, it helps to first understand the role of energy in a reaction.

Potential energy is stored in the chemical bonds of molecules. For a chemical reaction to occur, reactants must gain potential energy, often by absorbing heat from the environment. This added potential energy allows some bonds to break and new bonds to form as atoms are rearranged into products. Some energy is stored in products' bonds and some can be released back into the environment.

This added potential energy allows some bonds to break and new bonds to form as atoms are rearranged into products. Some energy is stored in products' bonds and some can be released back into the environment.

contents.text: In a chemical reaction, the starting molecules, or reactants, are converted into new molecules, or products. To understand how enzymes speed up chemical reactions, it helps to first understand the role of energy in a reaction.

Potential energy is stored in the chemical bonds of molecules. For a chemical reaction to occur, reactants must gain potential energy, often by absorbing heat from the environment. This added potential energy allows some bonds to break and new bonds to form as atoms are rearranged into products. Some energy is stored in products' bonds and some can be released back into the environment.
